chunks: Can ever man get what he desires?
ai.seo_question: What does the Quran mean when it asks if man will get what he desires?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often interpreted as a refutation of the Qadariyyah or those who claim absolute autonomy in achieving their desires, emphasizing that fulfillment is contingent upon Allah's will and decree. It highlights the distinction between mere human aspiration and the actualization of those desires through divine permission, serving as a reminder of human dependence on God. This rhetorical question underscores the theological principle that while humans possess free will, the ultimate outcome of their efforts remains subject to the Divine Decree.
